summary: Issue #467 steering: same disjoint infinite member chains, world-local causes and explanation labels admit two reason-truth assignments. The necessary always-true assignment fails the contrastive entailment standard; a contingent internal bearer passes. Thus neither infinite local coverage nor necessary reason truth alone determines discrimination. Internal explanation is not ruled out by externality assumptions; this candidate does not explain why its own contingent bearer obtains and may be rejected as explanatorily circular or merely redescriptive. Empty reason discovery coexists with a discriminator. No source reading revised; existing Leibniz attribution is only a target of comparison, not reinterpreted or formally refuted. Rejected bridges: treating local labels as modal sufficiency; deriving selection from necessity alone; identifying lack of discovery with nonexistence. General necessary_discriminating_excludes_rival derives incompatibility only with explicit necessity, discrimination and genuine accessible difference. See docs/history-contrastive-controls.md for exact boundaries, unresolved adequacy and total-history obligations. No root premise change.
